Mechanical implementation of the hybrid design principle for a teleoperable anthropomorphic hand (CRAFT Hand).
Assign three actuators to each finger to control (i) coupled flexion of the PIP and DIP joints, (ii) abduction/adduction of the MCP joint, and (iii) flexion/extension of the MCP joint.
Use a single tendon driving both PIP and DIP joints through a bidirectional TPU linkage that couples them with equal rotation.
Employ rolling contact joints at the PIP and DIP locations instead of pin joints for predictable motion and accurate modeling.
Integrate passive elastic bands to return PIP and DIP joints to neutral when tendon tension is released.
Use a cylindrical snap‑fit interface at the MCP joint for simplified assembly and breakage protection.
Design both MCP flexion/extension and abduction/adduction tendons to be backdrivable, allowing external forces to drive the transmission in reverse.
Implement modular finger design with metal dowel pins for easy swapping without disassembly or rewiring.
